blocks.text: Langley Farms: what the ground is and what governs it

items.t: The land base is the fact: 235 km² of the Township is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, so most Langley farm parcels are reserve land with Agricultural Land Commission housing and use rules layered over Township zoning. A specific parcel's reserve status is checked on the ALC maps by PID or civic address — never assumed from the district name.

Tenure: farm parcels are overwhelmingly freehold; strata farm product is not a Langley pattern: — no strata farm complex was confirmed on an official source, and on ALR land the form is barred outright. A Langley farm purchase is a fee-simple title purchase: Township zoning, ALR rules where the parcel is in the reserve, farm-class position, water rights and any registered covenants on title govern.

Soil capability: no agricultural capability class for the Township's main farm land was confirmed from a text source; capability is mapped per parcel in the BC Soil Information Finder, and the ALC soils page defines the classes from Class 1 (no or very slight limitations) through the lower classes. A parcel marketed on its soil class needs the per-parcel map read, not the listing's wording.

Farm classification is part of what trades: a parcel that keeps BC Assessment farm classification must keep meeting the minimum gross farm income thresholds, which scale with the size of the operation (full three-tier form). Sellers are advised to document the farm income history that supports the classification and any water licences or ALC approvals in place — those are the items a farm buyer's lender and lawyer will ask for first.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers

items.t: Zoning: Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 2500: applies across the Township; Township material names Rural Zones RU-1 and RU-2 and Suburban Residential Zones SR-1, SR-2 and SR-3. The minimum lot size for temporary farm labourer accommodation in Bylaw No. 2500 (s. 201.3) was not confirmed from a Township-hosted bylaw text — not confirmed. Read the parcel's own zone section before assuming any farm or home-based use is permitted.
R-CL compact lots: R-CL s.403 sets a 220 m² minimum lot area and a 464.5 m² maximum lot area (Township Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, s.403).

Water licensing: domestic groundwater use is exempt from licensing; groundwater used for non-domestic purposes such as irrigation requires a water licence under the Water Sustainability Act, and well records are searched in the GWELLS registry. An irrigated Langley farm bought without its licence position confirmed is bought with its core input unconfirmed.

If a strata purchase is made elsewhere in Langley (redirect case): the BC strata block applies — Form B diligence; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ units since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions) — a "45+" listing line is not a valid BC age bylaw. None of it applies to a Langley fee-simple farm purchase itself: no strata, no Form B, no strata fees.
The Township's SSMUH bylaw tops out at 4 units, so a Langley farm or lot should not be priced on a 6-plex assumption.

The R-CL figures are lot-area numbers. R-CL s.403 sets a 220 m² minimum and a 464.5 m² maximum lot area. There is no 355 m² figure in that section, either as a lot figure or as a floor-area cap (Township Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, s.403).

One hectare is 2.471 acres: The ALC additional-residence cap turns at 40 ha (≈98.8 acres) and the farm-class tiers at 0.8 ha and 4 ha; listings that blur the conversion blur which cap and which income tier apply to the parcel.

The farm area is township-wide, not one neighbourhood: the Township of Langley covers 316 square kilometres (km²), bounded by the Fraser River to the north and the United States border along 0 Avenue to the south.
Most farm land sits outside the six urban centres, in the rural area governed by the Rural Plan, Bylaw No. 3250.
The Fraser Valley Real Estate Board area is Langley; the municipality for these farms is the Township, not the separate City of Langley.
Three-quarters of the Township is farm land by designation: 75 per cent, or 235 km², is in the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR = Agricultural Land Reserve).
Parcels are mostly small for farm land: 73 per cent of Township ALR parcels are smaller than 4 hectares (ha), and only 14 per cent are larger than 8 ha, per the Agricultural Viability Strategy.
The main rural zone is Rural Zone RU-2 in Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, shown in a Council report as an 8.0 ha minimum lot size at 753 – 264 Street.
Half of all farms in Metro Vancouver are in this Township, per the Township agriculture page.

blocks.text: Langley Farms: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Subdivision, exclusion and non-farm use in the ALR need an Agricultural Land Commission (ALC = Agricultural Land Commission) application: the owner applies in the ALC Portal, the local government reviews it first, and the ALC decides if it is forwarded.
Small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH) does not open ALR farm land to multiplexes: ALR use stays under the Agricultural Land Commission Act and the Township rural zones above.
Normal farm practice is protected: a neighbour aggrieved by odour, noise or dust from a farm business applies to the BC Farm Industry Review Board (BCFIRB) for a normal farm practice determination.

blocks.text: Langley Farms: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Irrigation water is licensed, not automatic: the Water Sustainability Act requires a licence to divert, store or use surface or groundwater for non-domestic use, including agricultural use.
Irrigation equipment may lawfully operate 24 hours a day in the growing season, per the Province's Farm Practices Reference Guide irrigation factsheet.
The Township runs an Ecological Services Initiative with the Langley Sustainable Agriculture Foundation to help farmers bear the cost of keeping waterways and forests clean.
Farm questions go to a named Township contact: the Agricultural Planner, at cpp@tol.ca, per the Township agriculture page.

blocks.text: Langley Farms: development and new projects

items.t: ALR application, 753 – 264 Street and adjacent parcel: consolidation plus dedication of a gazetted portion of 8 Avenue in the ALR, owner application via Sager Nairne LLP, zoned RU-2. Status: Council report April 29, 2024 recommended forwarding to the ALC as compliant with Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 (as of November 3, 2026).
Agricultural Viability Strategy: Township strategy endorsed by Council in July 2013 to support farm viability. Status: endorsed 2013 (as of November 3, 2026).
The Township's total 2025 tax rate for Class 1 Residential was 3.34910 per $1,000 of assessed value, of which the total municipal rate was 1.87580, per the Township 2025 tax rates sheet.

Farm land is Class 9 only if it actually produces: BC Assessment states Class 9, Farm requires the land to produce a prescribed amount of qualifying primary agricultural products for sale; farm buildings fall in Class 1.

blocks.text: Langley Farms: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check ALR status parcel by parcel before subjects: the ALC application process page is the entry point, and the Township's own report for 753 – 264 Street confirms ALR status is stated separately from zoning and Rural Plan designation.
Check the water licence, not just the well: non-domestic groundwater use has required a licence since the Water Sustainability Act came into force on February 29, 2016.
The ALR map does not grant farm tax class: BC Assessment classifies on actual production for sale, not on ALR inclusion alone.

faq.q: Do I need a licence to use well water on a farm?
faq.a: Domestic groundwater use is exempt from licensing; groundwater used for non-domestic purposes such as irrigation requires a water licence under the Water Sustainability Act, and well records are searched in the GWELLS registry — older wells may not appear in it.

faq.q: How much of Langley is in the ALR?
faq.a: The Township of Langley states 235 square kilometres of the Township is within the Agricultural Land Reserve; check a specific parcel on the ALC maps.

faq.q: Can a Langley farm have a second dwelling?
faq.a: On ALR land, one additional residence is permitted without an ALC application where the conditions are met — 90 m² or less on parcels of 40 ha or smaller, 186 m² or less on larger parcels — and Township bylaws must also permit it.

faq.q: What is the ALR and does it apply to farms in Langley?
faq.a: The Agricultural Land Reserve is farmland protected by the provincial Agricultural Land Commission. Farm use is generally allowed on ALR land, but subdividing, adding homes or using the land for non-farm purposes usually needs approval, so check a property's ALR status before you offer.

faq.q: What should I check before buying a farm in Langley?
faq.a: Check the ALR status, water source and licences, drainage and flood history, the buildings and any quota or production licences that do or do not transfer with the land. Poultry and egg production in BC are supply-managed, so a sale of the farm does not automatically include quota.
